# POST /api/owners — Complete Create-Owner Flow

## 1-2. The endpoint

**Controller method:** `addOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)`
**File:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java:104-145`

The class `OwnerRestControllerV1` (`@RestController`, `@RequestMapping("/api")`, lines 56-59) implements the OpenAPI-generated interface `OwnersApi`. The POST mapping itself lives on the interface's default method:

- `/home/daniel/sandbox/target/generated-sources/openapi/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/api/OwnersApi.java:79-86` — `@RequestMapping(method = POST, value = "/owners", consumes/produces "application/json")`, so the effective path is `/api/owners`.

(Note: `OwnerRestControllerV2` exists but only implements `listOwnersPage` GET — it does **not** handle POST.)

## 3-4. Request body DTO and Bean Validation (fires FIRST, before controller body)

`@Valid @RequestBody OwnerFieldsDto` on the interface parameter (`OwnersApi.java:86`), plus the interface is annotated `@Validated` (`OwnersApi.java:44`). So Spring runs Bean Validation on the body before `addOwner` executes; failures throw `MethodArgumentNotValidException` → handled by the `@ControllerAdvice` (see §9), never reaching the controller.

**DTO:** `/home/daniel/sandbox/target/generated-sources/openapi/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/dto/OwnerFieldsDto.java`

Constraints in field-declaration order:

- **Class-level** `@ValidPostcode` — `OwnerFieldsDto.java:28` (custom, cross-field; see §7)
- **firstName** — `@NotNull @Pattern(^[\p{L}]+([ '-][\p{L}]+){0,2}$) @Size(1..30)` (`:86`)
- **lastName** — `@NotNull @Pattern(^[\p{L}]+([ '-][\p{L}]+){0,2}\.?$) @Size(1..30)` (`:107`)
- **address** — `@Pattern(^.*\S.*$) @Size(1..255)` (nullable) (`:128`)
- **addressLine1** — `@Pattern(^.*\S.*$) @Size(1..255)` (nullable) (`:149`)
- **addressLine2** — `@Pattern(^.*\S.*$) @Size(1..255)` (nullable) (`:170`)
- **city** — `@NotNull @Pattern(^.*\S.*$) @Size(1..80)` (`:191`)
- **telephone** — `@E164NationalLength` (field-level custom, `:43`) + `@NotNull @Pattern(...) @Size(1..20)` (`:212`)
- **email** — `@NonDisposableEmail` (field-level custom, `:46`) + `@Size(max 255) @Email` (`:233`)
- **postcode** — `@Pattern(^\d{4}$)` (nullable) (`:254`)
- **registrationDate** — `@PastOrPresent` (`:51`), `@Valid` (`:275`)
- **birthDate** — `@PastOrPresent` (`:55`), `@Valid` (`:296`)
- **sharesHousehold** — none
- **title** — `@Size(1..10)` (`:338`)

Note: `sharesHousehold` has a documented purpose ("allow creation even if same last name and address") but is **never read** anywhere in the controller/service — it is dead input.

## 5-6. Execution order inside the flow

Once validation passes and (`@PreAuthorize("hasRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN)")`, `:104`) authorization passes, execution proceeds. **Note on ordering:** an idempotency servlet filter wraps the whole thing (see §9) and runs before Spring MVC.

Ordered steps:

1. **Map DTO → entity** — `ownerMapper.toOwner(ownerFieldsDto)` (`:108`). The generated `OwnerMapperImpl.toOwner` (`/home/daniel/sandbox/target/generated-sources/annotations/.../OwnerMapperImpl.java:106-127`) calls setters in this order: firstName, lastName, title, registrationDate, birthDate, email, address, addressLine1, addressLine2, postcode, city, telephone. Several setters have **side effects** on the entity:
   - `setEmail` lower-cases the email (`Owner.java:205-207`)
   - `setAddress`/`setAddressLine1`/`setAddressLine2` normalize via `AddressNormalizer` and recompose `address` (`Owner.java:213-234`) — because address is set first then the lines, the final `address` is composed from the structured lines when present
   - `setTelephone` normalizes to E.164 via `PhoneNumbers.toE164` (`Owner.java:265-267`)
   - `id` and `pets` are explicitly ignored in the mapping (`OwnerMapper.java:50-51`)

2. **Registration-date business rule** — `BusinessDay.adjust(...)` rolls the given (or `LocalDate.now()`) date forward past weekends/holidays (`:109-111`, `BusinessDay.java:37-47`), then `owner.setRegistrationDate(adjusted)`.

3. **Load all owners** — `clinicService.findAllOwners()` filtered to non-deleted (`:112`). This is a `@Transactional(readOnly=true)` repo read (`ClinicServiceImpl.java:126-129`).

4. **Rate-limit check** — if ≥100 existing owners share the (adjusted) registration date → return **429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS**, no save (`:113-115`).

5. **Duplicate / city-capacity check** — if any existing owner has the same `identityKey` (hard duplicate), OR ≥50 owners already in the same city (case-insensitive) → return **409 CONFLICT**, no save (`:116-119`). `identityKey` = SHA-256 of normalized telephone + lower email + soundex(lastName) (`IdentityKey.java`, `Owner.java:139-142`).

6. **Derive and set entity fields (side effects on the entity), in order** (`:120-130`):
   - `setNamesakeCount(...)` — count of existing owners with same first+last name (case-insensitive)
   - `setHouseholdMemberCount(1 + count of same-household existing owners)` — household = same `householdId` (SHA of lastName+postcode, `HouseholdId.java`)
   - `setMemberId(MemberId.of(owner, owners))` — builds `<REGION><FY><HASH8><CHK>` and de-duplicates against existing member ids (`MemberId.java`)
   - `PossibleDuplicate.of(...)` then `setPossibleDuplicate(bool)` and `setPossibleDuplicateOf(id)` — soft-duplicate detection via soundex+postcode (`PossibleDuplicate.java`)
   - `setCapacityWarning(...)` — true if ≥40 owners already in same city

7. **PERSIST** — `clinicService.saveOwner(owner)` (`:131`) → `ownerRepository.save(owner)` in a `@Transactional` boundary (`ClinicServiceImpl.java:233-237`). This is where JPA lifecycle callbacks fire (see §8). `Pet` is `@OneToMany(cascade = ALL)` (`Owner.java:94-95`), but a newly created owner has no pets, so no cascade persists occur here.

8. **Map entity → response DTO** — `ownerMapper.toOwnerDto(owner)` (`:132`). Computes many derived read-only fields (membershipPoints/Level, ownerSegment, locality, timezone, ageBand, fiscalYear, identity, riskFlag, telephoneDisplay, contactPreference, selfLink) — see `OwnerMapper.java:22-37`.

9. **Post-save DTO adjustments** (do NOT touch the DB):
   - Cap `membershipLevel` at household max + 1 (`:133-139`)
   - `setBulkSignupWarning(...)` if >80 owners share the registration date (`:140-141`)

10. **Location header + response** — sets `Location: /api/owners/{id}` and returns **201 CREATED** with the DTO (`:142-144`).

## 7. Custom ConstraintValidators

- **`ValidPostcode`** (class-level on the DTO) — `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/validation/ValidPostcode.java` + `ValidPostcodeValidator.java`. When postcode present and city maps to a known region, enforces range NSW 2000-2099 / VIC 3000-3099 / QLD 4000-4099; absent postcode or unknown region passes.
- **`E164NationalLength`** (field, telephone) — `E164NationalLength.java` + `E164NationalLengthValidator.java`. Normalizes to E.164 and checks national-digit count per country code (+61→9, +1→10); unknown code or blank passes.
- **`NonDisposableEmail`** (field, email) — `NonDisposableEmail.java` + `NonDisposableEmailValidator.java`. Rejects domains mailinator.com / tempmail.com / guerrillamail.com; blank/absent/no-`@` passes.
- (Also present but unrelated to owner creation: `PetAgeValidator`.)

25. `setCapacityWarning(...)` — true if ≥40 owners in same city.

27. **INSERT** into DB. (Pets cascade `ALL`, but a new owner has none.)
28. **`@PostPersist onCreate(...)`** in `OwnerAuditListener`:
    - computes membershipLevel + ownerSegment

    - emits a structured JSON **`OWNER_CREATED` event** (monotonic `seq`, schemaVersion 2)
    - emits a **welcome notification** (`NOTIFY` logger)

29. **Entity → response DTO** (`toOwnerDto`) computing derived read-only fields (membership points/level, segment, locality, timezone, etc.).
30. **Cap `membershipLevel`** at household max + 1.
31. **Set `bulkSignupWarning`** if >80 owners share the registration date.
32. Set **`Location: /api/owners/{id}`** header, return **201 CREATED**.
33. The idempotency filter **caches/stores** the response if an `Idempotency-Key` was present.

**Cross-cutting:** the `CallMonitoringAspect` (`@Around` on `@Repository` beans) times/counts the repository calls for JMX during the reads and the save.

Note that no password encoding or role assignment happens here — those apply to the separate `User` entity, not `Owner`.
